messages:
noah: Hey team, first-week question  I grabbed a hosted sandbox API key from the console but my load test got a bunch of 429s. Where's the right place to ask for a dev quota bump or higher burst?
devex: welcome noah! :wave: For day-one dev use the sandbox key under Console -> API Keys -> Sandbox. Sandbox is intentionally rate-limited. Default is usually ~75k tokens/day and ~40 requests/min but it varies by account age.
noah: Got it. I'm running a short script hitting /v1/generate ~3 rps. Should I batch or file for higher burst?
kate: If this is local dev, batching or reducing concurrency is easiest. If you need a temporary higher burst for an experiment, request an ephemeral key via the quota form.
infra-bot: [infra-bot] Quota request form: https://internal.redwood.ai/quota-request. Choose "ephemeral dev key" for short-lived higher throughput. Include estimated tokens/day and duration.
noah: How long do ephemeral keys last and how do I create one?
devex: Ephemerals default to 24h (can be shorter). You can also self-create from CLI once approved: `rwd auth create-ephemeral --scopes=hosted:generate --ttl=24h`. They auto-expire.
noah: Any client retry guidance so I don't overload the sandbox?
security: Use exponential backoff with jitter (example: base 300ms, factor 2, cap 8s). Avoid tight loops and store keys in the vault. Never commit secrets to git.
noah: Are sandbox keys billed if I exceed quota?
devex: Sandbox is free within the quota. If you need permanent production access, you'll need a billing account and those keys are metered per-token. Temporary increases may require billing approval depending on volume.
noah: Cool. I'll try reducing concurrency and file the ephemeral request if needed. Thanks!
devex: If you're blocked, ping @devex in the form or DM and we fast-track new hires. Also here's a short runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/dev/onboarding-sandbox (includes example curl and retry snippet).
noah: Saved the runbook. Appreciate the help! :rocket:
